name: Philosophy
notes: Ten courses total (five named + five electives). IB higher-level score of 5+ awards PHIL 101 credit.
Optional emphases (law and ethics; history of philosophy; logic and philosophy of science) don't change the transcript; only the general requirements below are official.

Elective distribution constraints are partially modeled: at least three electives above PHIL 202 is enforced; the ethics course, the logic/traditional/phil-of-science course, and the advanced 'W' elective are represented as their own groups. 'No more than three logic-science courses' and the allied-field substitution are notes, not auto-checked.

requirementGroups.label: Core courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: PHIL 101: Introduction to Philosophy; PHIL 110: Intro Logic; PHIL 201: History of Ancient Philosophy; PHIL 202: History of Modern Philosophy; PHIL 393: Seminar for Majors

requirementGroups.label: Logic, traditional disciplines, or philosophy of science
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: At least one course from either logic and related courses (PHIL 211-219), or traditional philosophical disciplines (PHIL 242-249), or philosophy of science (PHIL 250-259).

requirementGroups.label: Advanced philosophy W course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: At least one advanced philosophy course designated with a 'W', to indicate upper-level writing credit.

requirementGroups.label: Advanced electives above PHIL 202 (3)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Five philosophy electives ... At least three courses must be above PHIL 202.

requirementGroups.label: Philosophy electives (2 more)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Five philosophy electives ... A relevant course in an allied field may be substituted for one of the five Philosophy electives above, with the permission of the Philosophy Department's undergraduate advisor.

upperLevelWriting.label: Advanced philosophy W course (fulfilled within the major)
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: At least one advanced philosophy course designated with a 'W', to indicate upper-level writing credit.
upperLevelWriting.note: The department states one advanced W course; the University's two-ULW-course norm is satisfied through the major's writing-intensive seminars per department policy.
